memos.headline: S06 Near Highs With Best Relative Strength; S05 and S01 in Persistent Downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. S06 stands out as the strongest name—just 0.6% off its 52-week high, +22.7% over 12 weeks, with 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +16.9% and a low ATR of 1.70%, signaling a steady, low-volatility uptrend. S04 has explosive momentum (+25.8% in 4 weeks, RSI 70.9) but is dangerously extended at +20% above its 50-day mean, making me cautious about chasing here. On the weak side, S05 is down 10.8% over 12 weeks with 12-week relative strength of -16.6% vs SPY and sits 14.1% off its high—this is a clear laggard I want to avoid. S01 is the only name trading below its 200-day mean (-2.2%), down 9.2% over 26 weeks, and showing persistent negative relative strength, which keeps me away until price reclaims the 200-day.

views.note: Closest to 52w high at -0.6%, best 12w relative strength (+16.9% vs SPY), low volatility ATR 1.70%; would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~340).
Massive 4w momentum (+25.8%) and strong relative strength, but RSI 70.9 and +20% above 50d mean screams overextension; wait for a pullback toward the 50d mean (~413) before getting long.
Healthy setup at +9% above 50d, only -4.5% from highs, RSI 63 not yet overbought, and positive 4w relative strength (+6.6%); would cut below 210.
Strong 1w bounce (+4.6%) and +8.5% above 50d, but 12w relative strength is -7.3% vs SPY, suggesting this is a mean-reversion bounce rather than a trend; need to see 12w RS turn positive.
Worst 12w relative strength in the universe at -16.6% vs SPY, -10.8% over 12 weeks, 14.1% drawdown from highs—clear downtrend; would reconsider only above 365.
Only name below its 200d mean (-2.2%), negative 26w return (-9.2%), and persistent negative relative strength; needs to reclaim 148 (200d area) to change my view.
4w return of -8.3% and worst 4w relative strength (-12.8% vs SPY) suggest accelerating weakness; 10% off highs with RSI 43.7 drifting lower—would reconsider above 320.
Deep 19.6% drawdown from highs and -6.1% below 50d mean, but still +13.5% above 200d; high ATR (4.40%) makes this a coin-flip—need a reclaim of the 50d (~912) to get constructive.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Explosive Earnings Growth; S09 and S01 Flash Margin and Growth Warnings
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between names with durable, accelerating earnings power and those showing cash-flow compression or stagnation. S10 posted 85.2% YoY revenue growth and a 71.5% net margin on $81.6B of revenue with only $8.5B in total debt—this is the cleanest high-growth profile in the group. S05 is similarly extraordinary: $119.8B in revenue at a 93.7% net margin with net income up nearly 298% YoY and minimal leverage ($14.8B debt). On the other end, S09's net income fell 45.8% YoY to just $4.2B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin with revenue barely growing at 2.4%, and S01 saw net income decline 15.8% on only 1.5% revenue growth with a 14.4% margin and $29.3B in debt—both signal deteriorating earnings power. S03 deserves attention for its 244.9% net income surge and 31.2% margin on $200.6B revenue, though $133B in debt warrants monitoring; a margin reversal there would change my view quickly.

views.note: 85% revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, negligible leverage ($8.5B debt)—best earnings trajectory in the universe; would reassess if margins compress below 50%.
93.7% net margin and 298% YoY net income growth on $119.8B revenue with very low debt make this a standout; any margin normalization below 70% would be a red flag.
39.7% net margin, 17.7% revenue growth, 31.3% net income growth, and manageable $40.3B debt reflect durable, high-quality earnings.
$200.6B revenue growing 19.6% with net income up 244.9% is compelling, but $133B in total debt means I need to see margin stability above 25% to stay constructive.
24% revenue growth and 64.9% net income growth are solid, but 17.5% margin and $36.2B debt on only $20.5B revenue leave limited margin of safety.
27.7% revenue growth and 36.9% margin are attractive, but $460.5B in total debt is an outsized liability that could compress equity returns if rates stay elevated.
$109.4B revenue growing 16.4% with 27.2% margin is respectable, but $82.3B debt and slower net income growth (27.1%) relative to peers temper enthusiasm.
Flat revenue (+0.4%), 4.9% net margin, and $73.3B in debt signal weak pricing power; the 61% net income bounce looks like a low-base effect, not durable improvement.
Net income down 45.8% YoY to $4.2B on a 4.9% margin with only 2.4% revenue growth—clear earnings deterioration with no near-term catalyst visible.
Revenue growth of just 1.5%, net income declining 15.8%, and $29.3B debt on $21.2B revenue point to shrinking earnings power; would reconsider only if margins recover above 18%.

memos.headline: Fed Paused at 3.75% but Sticky 3.5% YoY CPI and Rising Long Yields Argue Against Duration and Favor Banks Over Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode—upper bound at 3.75%, unchanged over three months despite 75bp of cuts over the past year. CPI is running at 3.5% YoY with the labor market tightening (unemployment at 4.10%, down 20bp over both 3m and 12m horizons), which removes any urgency for further easing. The 10y yield at 4.68% has climbed 21bp in three months and 39bp over the year, while the 10y-2y spread sits at +48bp, a positively sloped but flattening curve. This regime—paused policy, above-target inflation, solid employment, and rising long rates—is hostile to duration-sensitive growth equities and supportive of banks earning healthy net interest margins. A CPI print dropping below 3.0% or unemployment rising above 4.4% would shift my regime call toward renewed easing expectations.

views.note: Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve (10y-2y +48bp) and a paused Fed keeping short rates stable while long rates grind higher.
Cyclicals are supported by a tightening labor market (UE 4.10%, -20bp 3m) signaling resilient demand in a no-recession backdrop.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from the 10y yield at 4.68% and rising, with no near-term easing catalyst.
Long-duration bond proxies and rate-sensitive names are pressured as 10y yields rose 39bp YoY with sticky inflation at 3.5%.
Staples offer defensive positioning but limited upside in a resilient economy; their bond-like characteristics are a drag with rising long yields.
Energy benefits from a solid demand backdrop (low unemployment) and acts as an inflation hedge with CPI still at 3.5% YoY.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S03 and S04 Surge While S08 and S05 Slide on Results
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions as the clearest sentiment signal across the universe right now. S03 (+15.3%) and S04 (+15.5%) posted outsized positive reactions to their late-July results filings, suggesting a genuine narrative shift that likely has further room to run given the magnitude of the moves. Conversely, S08 (-7.4%) and S05 (-7.1%) saw sharp negative reactions on their results, and with no subsequent positive catalysts in the filing record, the negative tone appears entrenched. S07's +5.6% reaction on its Aug 4 results is more modest but still constructive, while S01's -1.9% on Q4 results alongside multiple same-day filings (including a director departure) reads as mildly negative but not alarming. S09's July 1 filing flagging delisting risk and material rights modifications is a red flag that I would not fade.

views.note: A +15.3% earnings-day reaction signals a powerful positive narrative shift that likely has legs.
The +15.5% post-results move is the strongest in the universe and suggests sentiment has decisively turned positive.
A -7.4% earnings reaction with no subsequent positive filings leaves negative sentiment intact.
The -7.1% results reaction and a subsequent 'Other Events' filing without a clear positive catalyst keep tone negative.
A +5.6% earnings reaction is constructive though more modest; positive tone but less conviction than S03/S04.
Delisting risk and material rights modifications flagged in the July 1 filing represent a severe negative narrative.
A mild +2.5% earnings reaction and heavy corporate-action filing volume suggest stable but unremarkable sentiment.
A -1.9% Q4 reaction paired with a director departure is mildly negative but not decisive enough to take a directional view.

memos.headline: Declining Policy Uncertainty and Subdued VIX Suggest Geopolitical Tail Risks Are Fading, but Oil Volatility Warrants Caution
memos.body: I see a broadly benign geopolitical backdrop as of mid-August 2026: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has fallen ~18% over three months to 193.83, VIX is at 14.63 (down ~18% over the same window), and HY spreads remain tight at 2.71%. The one wrinkle is WTI crude, which rose 4.5% month-over-month to $82.77 even as it is still down ~21% over three months—suggesting a possible near-term supply disruption or OPEC discipline that could re-inject energy-security risk. Without specific GDELT event data on sanctions, export controls, or China-policy escalation in the evidence set, I cannot identify a structural geopolitical shift; the 8-K filings from S01, S03, S05, S06, and S07 are generic Other Events or Reg FD disclosures that do not flag supply-chain or policy-related material changes. My base case is that the current calm persists unless we see a new sanctions package or export-control action, which would change my view on semiconductor and energy-exposed names.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in two months signal active corporate communication but none indicate geopolitical exposure; staying neutral until content clarifies.
Multiple Reg FD disclosures in late July suggest investor outreach but no geopolitical red flags in the available evidence.
Recent 8-K (Aug 10) is an Other Events filing with no detail on sanctions or supply-chain risk; low conviction either way.
Single July 8-K with no geopolitical content discernible; declining policy uncertainty supports a benign read.
Reg FD disclosure in early August is uninformative on policy risk; no basis to take a directional view.
With WTI down 21% over three months and policy uncertainty easing, energy-cost-sensitive names may benefit if no new sanctions emerge.
No company-specific filings or geopolitical catalysts in the evidence; defaulting to neutral given the calm macro backdrop.

plan.summary: Overweight the strongest consensus longs (S06, S03, S04, S10) where multiple analysts agree on favorable technicals, fundamentals, or sentiment, while keeping meaningful cash given rising long yields and S04's overextension risk. Avoid names with deteriorating earnings, negative relative strength, or adverse sentiment (S05, S01, S08, S09).

plans.rationale: Strongest technical setup in the universe (0.6% from 52w high, best 12w relative strength, low ATR) and macro tailwind from positively sloped yield curve benefiting banks. Fundamentals are decent (27.7% revenue growth, 36.9% margin) though large debt noted. Sentiment mild but not negative.
